purpose: Track RWAMOD (SOUTHMOD Rwanda) model findings and grounding gaps observed in household-level Axiom oracle comparisons, mirroring ghamod_issues.json, microzamod_issues.json and etmod_issues.json. Canonical narrative ledger: rulespec-rw#1 closing comment.

observed_with.dataset: rw_2024_a1 (registered name; synthetic rows - the bundle ships no Rwandan microdata)

entries.summary: RWAMOD RW_2025 applies the informal-sector CBHI member premiums by monthly-earnings tier (probed 2026-10-04: 250 FRW per month up to 30,000 FRW of monthly earnings, 416.67 to 60,000, 666.67 to 120,000 and 1,666.67 above, i.e. 3,000/5,000/8,000/20,000 FRW per year; zero with no earnings) for CY2025, where the first gazetted carrier of the schedule is Ministerial Order No 002/26/10/TC of 16/02/2026 (Official Gazette no Special of 23/02/2026, in force on publication; expressed by IMIBEREHO Dynamic Social Registry level). The prior gazetted instrument (PM Order No 105/03 of 30/09/2020) carries the funding schedule and the 0.5% employee levy but no income-tier member premiums; the income-tier practice ran administratively from 2024 under RSSB publication (the RWAMOD report's own citation). The amounts agree; the validation-year grounding does not. The rulespec-rw module starts 2026-02-23, so the rw-cbhi-tiers suite is a period-shifted schedule check (Axiom at 2027 against RWAMOD RW_2025; 4/4 live on 2026-10-04), and the pairing of each earnings point with a registry level is a suite assumption, not a sourced mapping.

RWAMOD applies a 2% employer occupational-hazards contribution (tscerac_s, probed 2026-10-04: 2,000.00 at uprated monthly employment income 100,000). Law No 06/2003 (modifying the Decree-Law of 22 August 1974) Article 10 makes the branch exclusively employer-paid and Article 9 delegates the percentage rates to a Presidential Decree that is not publicly digitized (the RSSB scheme page documents benefits, not the rate; the RWAMOD report itself cites the RSSB webpage). No encodable primary carrier exists, so the 2% stays a documented grounding gap - the framework law is captured and the rate is not encoded.

RWAMOD taxes bottled-water expenditure at 10% (tex11_s; probed 2026-10-04: 10% of the item's post-uprating value) for the whole of RW_2025, where Law No 011/2025 of 27/05/2025 (in force on publication, 29/05/2025) carries NO water row in its Annex - the row existed in the repealed Law No 050/2023, in force through 28 May 2025. The model otherwise applies the 2025 schedule (cigarettes 36% plus FRW 230 per pack, wine 40%; both probed 2026-10-04), so the year mixes the new rates with a dropped row. The rulespec-rw excise module encodes the 2025 Annex only.

RWAMOD prices every item in its juice expenditure basket at 10% (tex09_s; probed 2026-10-04: 10% of each item's post-uprating value), where the Law 011/2025 Annex prices only juices with at least 30% local raw material content at 10% (item 1) and other juices at 39% (item 2). Basket-level simplification: the survey data cannot split local content, so the model applies the local rate to all juice.

RWAMOD prices its local-beer expenditure basket at the 40% local-beer rate (tex06_s) and one other-beer item at 65% (tex07_s) (probed 2026-10-04: 40% and 65% of the post-uprating values), where the Law 011/2025 Annex separately prices other fermented beverages at 65% (item 11) and other alcoholic beverages with local raw material content at 30% (item 12) - traditional or fermented drinks inside the 40% basket are not distinguished. Basket-level simplification recorded for the excise dispositions.

RWAMOD charges a RAMA medical contribution on old-age pension income for persons flagged as pensioners (tscpehl_s): probed live on 2026-10-03 and again on 2026-10-04, at uprated monthly pension income (poa) of 100,000 and 400,000 with the pensioner flag poayn=1 it returns tscpehl_s 7,500 and 30,000 (7.5%) and reduces ils_dispy by the same amount; with poayn=0 it returns 0. The rulespec-rw RAMA module (rw/statutes/law-2001-24/rama-contributions) encodes the Article 44 contribution on the employee's basic salary only and records that its captured print (the RSSB library English consolidated print of Law No 24/2001 incorporating Law No 29/2002) carries no provision extending contributions to retired members, leaving the pensioner arm to a parity disposition. Unadjudicated: no gazetted carrier for a pensioner contribution has been identified or ruled out, so this is not yet classified as a model or encoding gap. No rw suite runs a pensioner case.

RWAMOD charges VAT twice on the bottled-water item. Probed 2026-10-04 on a row with 10,000 FRW per month of bottled-water spend and nothing else: the echoed VAT base il_exp_vat01 holds the post-uprating 10,977.19, the water excise tex11_s is 1,097.72 (10%), and tva_s is 4,149.38 = 18% of 10,977.19 (1,975.89, the standard-rated VAT base) plus 18% of 10,977.19 + 1,097.72 (2,173.48, the VAT the model adds on every excisable purchase's value plus excise). A juice item at the same spend, whose spend does not show up in il_exp_vat01 (observed), carries only the second amount. Law No 049/2023 Article 4 charges VAT once on the taxable value, so the water item's effective VAT (37.8% of the post-uprating value) has no statutory basis whichever of the two bases is right. No rw suite compares VAT on an excisable good, so nothing mismatches today.

RWAMOD reads the same expenditure value two incompatible ways. Probed 2026-10-04 on a row with 20,000 FRW per month of cigarette spend and 10 packs and nothing else: tex01_s is 10,295.12 = 36% of the post-uprating spend (22,208.67) plus 230 x 10, which reads the spend as the tax-inclusive retail price the Law 011/2025 Annex names; tva_s is 5,850.68 = 18% of the spend plus that excise, which reads the same spend as a value before excise and VAT. On a single food item tva_s is 18% of the post-uprating spend (2,048.77 on 11,382.06), again reading spend as VAT-exclusive. At most one reading can match how a household's recorded spending relates to Law No 049/2023's taxable value and the Annex's tax-inclusive retail price. The rw-* suites adopt the model's reading per tax for parity and test rates, not base definitions: rw-vat feeds the post-uprating spend as the module's taxable_value, and rw-excise feeds it as the module's cigarette_retail_value (the tax-inclusive retail price). Unadjudicated.
